risk_if_not_implemented: Without Security, Compliance & Resilience Outsourcing Limitations, supplier and External Service Provider (ESP) weaknesses, incidents or failures may propagate into the organization's environment unmanaged. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Uncontrolled Third-Party Security / Privacy Exposure (R-GV-5), Lack of oversight of third-party controls (R-GV-7), Unreliable Assurance / Decision Information (R-GV-10), Third-Party Legal / Compliance Exposure (R-SC-4), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Statutory / Regulatory / Contractual Change (MT-11).

compensating_control_1.name: Third-Party Services
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to mitigate the risks associated with third-party access to the organization's Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD).
compensating_control_1.justification: Third-Party Services (TPM-12) provides third-party oversight and contractual controls that compensates for the absence of Security, Compliance & Resilience Outsourcing Limitations (TPM-05) by extending security obligations and monitoring third-party risk in lieu of direct primary control implementation. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Control Inheritance
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to define instances of control inheritance within assessment boundaries.
compensating_control_2.justification: Control Inheritance (CPL-15) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Security, Compliance & Resilience Outsourcing Limitations (TPM-05) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
